teaser: Footprint is what an agent actually did, read afterwards from logs and vault history; blast radius is what a row of its reach would cost the business today.
core_idea: Add two words to the Agent Behaviour Policy: footprint, what the agent actually did, read afterwards from the record and compared with the mandate, and blast radius, what a row of its reach would cost the business if used in full today, with whether there is a way back.

nodes.label: Reach, mandate, gap and barriers
nodes.summary: RiskMandate's policy is written before the agent runs: reach is what it can do, mandate what you asked, gap the difference in both directions, barriers what stands in the way.

nodes.label: Only a boundary is a control
nodes.summary: A barrier is a boundary, a setting, an expectation or nothing, and most of what organisations call controls turn out to be expectations once they are typed.

nodes.label: Footprint
nodes.summary: The set of things the agent actually did, in a period, read from the record afterwards; the same kind of list as the reach and the mandate, but evidence rather than a decision.

nodes.label: Where the footprint comes from
nodes.summary: The connector's audit log, the model provider's tool-call record, a connector twin's replay, a vault's commit history, the append lanes and the agents' own messages.

nodes.label: Reading, not intercepting
nodes.summary: Nothing sits inline, a copy of the logs or a read key is enough so an outside reviewer can do it, and the footprint accumulates so some findings only exist at the twelfth week.

nodes.label: Footprint in the gap
nodes.summary: The agent did something within its reach and outside its mandate and nothing stopped it, which is a near miss, and it resolves by adding the row to the mandate or putting a boundary in front of it.

nodes.label: Dormant mandate
nodes.summary: A row the owner asked for that the footprint never shows: an over-stated mandate, a check that was relied on and never ran, or a shortfall the reach inventory missed.

nodes.label: Expected-use hint
nodes.summary: Each mandate row wants a hint of how often the owner expects to see it, always, sometimes, rarely, hopefully never, so a dormant row can be told from a contingency that was never needed.

nodes.label: The mandate as practised
nodes.summary: Read the footprint for a month and you have the rows the agent actually uses, with the near misses marked, as the first draft of a policy for an agent that has none.

nodes.label: Blast radius
nodes.summary: What it would cost the business if a row were used in full, today, defined over the reach because whoever takes the agent over inherits its reach and ignores its mandate.

nodes.label: Whether there is a way back
nodes.summary: Two rows with the same scope and different reversibility are not the same risk, and the policy should say so.

nodes.label: Same footprint, different blast radius
nodes.summary: An agent drops a staging table three times over two months; the row is identical each time, and only on day forty-one, when it held six weeks of real records, is it the incident.

nodes.label: What the cloud already does
nodes.summary: AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Entra already compare permissions granted with permissions used, but a permission set carries no statement of intent, so there is no dormant mandate.

nodes.label: A vault is a footprint recorder by construction
nodes.summary: Every commit is signed, versioned and append-only, so an agent working in a vault leaves a footprint whether or not anyone intended to collect one, and most of what sgit does shrinks the irreversible part of the blast radius.

nodes.label: The gap plus blast radius is the risk
nodes.summary: The gap is exposure, blast radius is impact, and the person who accepts a gap is accepting its blast radius, which until now the policy did not state.

nodes.label: Reading our own footprint
nodes.summary: Ten agents, six with a written policy, eight days of commit history; the footprint against the six policies is still to be read and published as the second article.

quotes.text: The mandate tells you what you hoped for. The reach tells you what you are exposed to.
quotes.why: Why blast radius is defined over the reach, not the mandate: an attacker inherits the reach.

quotes.text: The footprint is how you get near misses for agents without waiting for the luck to run out.
quotes.why: The payoff of reading the footprint against the gap: incidents and near misses are the same events with different luck.
